title: MS-003.4 — Pure Construct function (shared by validate/plan/generate)
description:
## Goal
Implement pure `construct(effective_inputs, catalog) -> Plan` with no I/O beyond what is already
loaded into memory. Domain logic lives in plan/resolve/spec — not only in cli.

## Why
INV-3 / REQ-040: generate must not silently diverge from plan Construct for same effective inputs.
This is the single source of planned file sets.

## Architecture
- Input: effective inputs + catalog view (stub catalog OK: minimal fixture file set)
- Output: immutable Plan
- Path jail checks for planned paths (REQ-053) should hard-fail at construct when paths escape
- No imports of fsx/generate/cli

## Stub catalog strategy
Until MS-007, Construct may plan a minimal fixture tree (e.g. README + Cargo.toml skeleton) so
pipeline and goldens can exist. Document stub clearly; replace with embed later without changing
Construct signature.

## Acceptance

title: MS-003.1 — Normalize effective inputs (spec + overrides → Construct input)
description:
## Goal
Single function (or pure pipeline step) that takes parsed ProjectSpec + CLI overrides and produces
**normalized effective inputs** used by all of validate/plan/generate.

## Why
REQ-034: overrides apply **before** Construct. REQ-040 equality is on effective inputs after overrides
and after resolve normalization (profile order later; v1 profiles already validated at parse).

## Scope
- Apply --name / --dest / --verify with CLI-wins precedence
- Default verify mode when omitted (document: typically `default` at generate; plan should record effective mode)
- Keep pure: no FS writes
- Surface stable errors if overrides invalid

## Acceptance
Unit tests: flag wins over TOML; missing optional verify handled; name/dest empty rejected if applicable.

## Out of scope
Profile membership CLI overrides (explicitly none in v1).
design: Single pure normalization step after parse. REQ-034 requires CLI-over-TOML before Construct so plan-as-contract (REQ-040) stays enforceable. Profile membership has no CLI override in v1.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests: --name/--dest/--verify win over TOML when present
- Missing optional verify handled with documented default for Construct recording
- Empty name rejected; pure function (no FS writes)
- Output type is the single Construct input used by validate/plan/generate paths

title: MS-005 — Stage, place, generate lifecycle
description:
## Outcome
`foundry generate` stages render output, optional stub verify hook, exclusive place; lifecycle table
per REQ-050.

## Architecture
- `render` produces pure path→bytes map (BTreeMap or equivalent)
- `fsx` writes map into stage root transactionally; place prefers same-FS rename; cross-device fail-closed
- `generate` orchestrates: Construct → (assert plan_sha256 matches contract) → stage → verify hook → place
- On Construct/plan digest mismatch vs independent construct: **fail before any FS write**

## Lifecycle (REQ-050)
| Outcome | Destination | Stage |
| Render fail | Untouched | Retained |
| Verify fail | Untouched | Retained; path in error |
| Place success | Complete tree | Cleaned |
| Place fail | Fail-closed | Retained |

## Prerequisites
MS-004 (stable plan shapes)

## Blocks
MS-006 (full matrix)

## REQs
REQ-050,051,052,053 (initial place + jail); REQ-020 generate; verify may be stub

## Explicit non-goals
Real cargo verify (PHASE-03); full catalog emit (PHASE-02)

## Risks
RSK-100 destructive overwrite; RSK-112 stage leftovers; RSK-109 path escape
acceptance_criteria:
- generate stages then exclusive place
- Success cleans stage; fail retains stage and prints path
- Dest never partially written on render/verify fail
- Construct digest mismatch fails before FS write
- No merge/update commands

comments.author: Robert Guss
comments.text:
## Write path architecture reminder

render → pure map; fsx → stage + exclusive place; generate → orchestrate with Construct digest assert **before any FS write**.
Cross-device place: fail-closed unless future DEC adds copy+swap. Never merge-default.

title: MS-005.3 — fsx: exclusive place algorithm (REQ-051)
description:
## Goal
Implement admissibility + place:
- missing path OK; empty dir (zero read_dir children) OK
- non-empty (incl .git), file-at-path, symlink → refuse, dest unchanged
- Prefer atomic rename same-FS; EXDEV → fail-closed with clear error (no silent copy+swap without DEC)

## Why
INV-2 / Blueprint non-goal of merge-default. FND-002 made emptiness testable.

## Acceptance
Unit tests for each admissibility class (full matrix formalized in MS-006).

title: MS-004 — SPK-100 golden plan freeze
description:

## Why before generate (MS-005)
FND-200 / plan rule: if generate invents fixture shapes first, plan JSON becomes accidental API.
SPK-100 freezes the contract agents and CI will snapshot.

## Method

`cargo insta review` accepted update path; redact unstable catalog digests.

## Prerequisites

## Acceptance

error JSON shape included in fixtures.

## Future-self note
After this milestone, additive renames of plan JSON keys need tests and conscious migration.
Do not "drive-by" rename fields in generate work.

comments.author: Robert Guss
comments.text:
## SPK-100 discipline

After this milestone, plan JSON keys are a public fixture contract. Use insta (or equivalent) + redaction for catalog digests. Document field names so PHASE-02 golden extensions do not invent parallel schemas.

title: MS-003.3 — Plan data model covering REQ-041 element set

## Goal

foundry version + catalog digest; validated/normalized spec; resolved composition;
planned files (path, mode, content digest); dependency/Cargo.toml deltas; AI-native paths;
verify mode; destination policy decision; plan_sha256; warnings.

## Why
Reviewability and contract tests. Exact **JSON field names** may still refine under SPK-100 (MS-004);
element **set** is Must now (REQ-041).

## Design considerations
- Use content digests (sha256) for planned file bytes even if render is stubbed
- plan_sha256 over canonical serialization of plan semantic content
- Destination policy: missing / empty-admissible / refuse (predicate per REQ-051; no place yet)
- Catalog digest may be placeholder until MS-007 embed

## Acceptance

title: MS-003 — Pure Construct `plan` command
description:
## Outcome
`foundry plan` emits text/JSON plan elements; zero destination writes; CLI overrides applied in
Construct path before pure construction; plan package remains pure.

## Why this milestone exists
Plan-as-contract (INV-3 / REQ-040) is the trust core for agents: dry-run must match what generate
will place. Overrides must not create a second ad-hoc path (FND-001 → REQ-034).

## Architecture gate
`src/plan/` MUST NOT import crate::fsx, crate::generate, crate::cli (or foundry:: equivalents).
Enforce with crate structure and/or source-scan test (tests/purity.rs already seeds this).

## Error contract
Stable error codes for validation/override/plan failures in both text and JSON (`--format json`).

## REQs
REQ-020 (plan command), REQ-022,023,034,040–043; supports REQ-041 elements (names freeze at MS-004)

## Prerequisites
MS-002 (spec parse/validate + overrides surface)

## Blocks
MS-004 only (not MS-005 directly — SPK-100 freezes JSON first).

## Acceptance evidence

- Write-free sandbox: plan does not mutate dest

description:
## Goal
Stand up the Rust Foundry product crate with lifecycle commands, pure Construct shared by
validate/plan/generate, and fail-closed write path (stage → verify-hook point → exclusive place).

## User-visible outcome
Non-interactive `foundry validate|plan|generate` against a TOML Project Spec with CLI overrides;
destination never partially written; non-empty destinations refuse.

## Why this phase is first
Write safety (REQ-050/051/053 + SPK-101) and plan-as-contract (REQ-034/040 + SPK-100) must exist
**before** catalog breadth. Expanding templates on an unsafe write path or divergent plan/apply
is the highest structural risk (RSK-100, RSK-101).

## REQs (phase coverage)
REQ-001,002,003,020–024,030–034,040–043,050–053,130

## Normative ordering rule
**No plan JSON field names treated as stable until MS-004 (SPK-100).** MS-005 must not freeze
public plan JSON shape before MS-004. DAG: MS-003 → MS-004 → MS-005 → MS-006 (FND-200).

## Exit criteria (observable)
1. Product crate builds on Linux CI; no Windows jobs
2. validate/plan/generate exist; non-interactive; documented exit codes
3. Same effective inputs → equal planned file sets; cross-command plan_sha256 equality
4. SPK-100 golden + SPK-101 matrix green (MS-004 before MS-005 shapes)
5. Path jail fixtures hard-fail escapes
6. plan-package purity scan green
7. Stable error codes for denylist, schema, archetype, path-jail, non-empty, file-at-path, symlink, place failure
8. Destination never partially placed on failure; stage path printed on fail
9. Module map inspectable (REQ-130 Should)

## Explicit non-goals this phase
Full embedded Core matrix (PHASE-02); real default verify runners (PHASE-03 — stub OK);
AI-native content (PHASE-04); full acceptance suite (PHASE-05).

## Rollback triggers
If exclusive place cannot be correct without merge: **stop** — do not ship merge-default.
If Construct cannot be shared: reconsider before catalog expansion (INV-3).

title: rust-foundry v1 — Product delivery (hybrid Foundry)
description:
## Goal
Deliver the **rust-foundry** product: a planner-led Rust CLI hybrid foundry that turns a
declarative TOML Project Spec into a complete single-crate Rust CLI (optional TUI/hooks/secrets/distribution
profiles) via **validate → plan → generate**, with a strong Core, closed embedded catalog, fail-closed
writes, portable AI-native surfaces, and a catalog-SoT GitHub template snapshot.

## Over-arching product vision (Blueprint)
Personal, open-sourceable, **AI-native hybrid foundry** for modern Rust CLI/TUI projects:
1. Generator CLI (validate / plan dry-run / generate)
2. Strong default Core (toolchain, layout, quality gates, CI, agent surface)
3. Optional profiles (CLI primary; TUI optional — not forced into every CLI)
4. GitHub template surface for pure-CLI onboarding
5. Agent-first operability without oral tradition
6. Teach-as-you-go legibility (owner has less Rust depth than Go/Python)

## Authority ladder (do not invent REQs)
1. Accepted DEC-### (none at plan time; check decisions/)
2. Blueprint locks & non-goals (`docs/00-program-blueprint.md`)
3. **Revised definitive specification** = product law (`docs/02-definitive-specification-revised.md`)
4. **Revised implementation plan** = delivery sequence (`docs/02-implementation-plan-revised.md`)
5. Product AGENTS.md / README = workflow only; never override REQs
Pinned research commits: see `docs/AUTHORITY.md`.

## Delivery structure (normative DAG)
PHASE-01 → PHASE-02 → (PHASE-03 // PHASE-04 draft) → PHASE-05
Milestone critical path:
MS-001 → MS-002 → MS-003 → MS-004 → MS-005 → MS-006
→ MS-007 → MS-008 → MS-021 → MS-009 → MS-010 → MS-011
→ MS-012 → MS-013 → MS-014 → MS-015
→ MS-016 → MS-017 → MS-018
→ MS-019 → MS-020

Special join rules:
- **No plan JSON field names stable until MS-004 (SPK-100)** before MS-005 generate shapes.
- **MS-021 pure-CLI dogfood before** MS-009/MS-010 profile/TUI expansion (FND-203).
- MS-016 may draft after MS-011 in parallel with PHASE-03; **MS-018 / PHASE-04 exit** require
  REQ-088 string-match vs MS-012 + MS-013 freeze fixtures (FND-201).
- PHASE-05 ship gate is **REQ-150/151 scenario checklist**, not bare "CI green" (FND-202).

## Product locks (never silently undo)
- macOS + Linux only; **never Windows** (L3 / REQ-003)
- Exclusive place; refuse non-empty default; no merge-default generate (INV-2 / REQ-051/052)
- Closed catalog; offline catalog ≠ offline verify (INV-1 / REQ-060 vs REQ-120)
- AGENTS.md + `.agents/skills/` only; no Claude Core; MCP default none (L7 / REQ-006/007)
- Plan-as-contract: same pure Construct for validate/plan/generate (INV-3 / REQ-040)
- Catalog SoT for GH template (INV-4 / REQ-122)
- Product code in this product repo only (L12 / REQ-010) — research repo is not implementation

## Secret field denylist (REQ-033)
Case-insensitive field **names** (any nesting): password, secret, token, api_key, private_key,
access_key, client_secret.

## Package layout (spec §10.1)
src/{main,lib,cli,spec,catalog,resolve,plan,report,render,fsx,generate,verify}
**Purity:** `plan` MUST NOT import fsx, generate, or cli.

## Current delivery position (as of bead graph creation)
- PHASE-01 in progress
- **MS-001 complete** (bootstrap) — evidence: docs/evidence/MS-001-bootstrap.md
- **MS-002 complete** (validate + schema 1 + denylist) — evidence: docs/evidence/MS-002-spec-validate.md
- **Next: MS-003** Pure Construct `plan` command

## Definition of done (local engineering)
cargo build/test; cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy -- -D warnings; cargo run -- version; just ci when wired.
Phase/milestone exit criteria from the revised plan before claiming phase done.
No secret material in Project Specs or goldens.

## How to use this bead graph
- Work topologically: `bd ready` surfaces unblocked open work.
- Prefer children under milestones; close children before closing milestones/epics.
- Descriptions are self-contained contracts for agents — do not treat chat history as authority.

comments.author: Robert Guss
comments.text:
## Beads graph edge semantics (learned)

When using `bd create --graph`, edges of type `blocks` are stored as:
- `from_key` **depends on** `to_key` (i.e. `to_key` blocks `from_key`)

So to express "A must finish before B", use:
```json
{"from_key": "B", "to_key": "A", "type": "blocks"}
```
Equivalent CLI: `bd dep add B A` or `bd dep A --blocks B`.

This graph was corrected post-import to the normative delivery DAG.
